newsitem.title: INDONESIA: NEC gets Indonesia telecommunication deal.
newsitem.headline: NEC gets Indonesia telecommunication deal.

text.p: NEC Corporation of Japan said on Monday its Indonesian subsidiary had obtained a contract worth some five billion yen for a public switching system.
"NEC Corporation and PT Humpuss have jointly received an order for the third-phase public switching system project of PT Telkom in Indonesia," NEC said in a statement.

NEC said PT NEC Nusantara Communications, a joint venture between NEC and PT Humpuss, a company controlled by President Suharto's youngest son, had employed Sumitomo Corporation as the main contractor and the Suppliers Credit of the Japan Export and Import Bank for the project financing.
It said NEC will begin supplying 263,000 lines to the areas in and around Jakarta, Surabaya and other cities in east Java by the end of this month.
Indonesia targeted to install public switching systems with a minimum of five million telephone lines by the end of its current sixth five-year development plan ending in 1999.
